task: Write one sentence of your own using the word scathing. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know scathing should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The coach's halftime verdict was scathing enough that even the seniors studied their cleats like freshmen.
Cutting is milder than scathing — one sharp stroke, quickly over.
Savage is fiercer than scathing: a scathing review is a scalpel with intent, while a savage one stops pretending to be surgery.

Withering is scorn that makes its target shrivel on the spot — a look, a tone, a single raised eyebrow can carry it. Scathing is wounding criticism carried in words, composed and sustained across sentences or pages. Withering strikes in an instant; scathing builds its case and leaves scars.

Caustic criticism burns like acid — its signature is corrosive, sarcastic bite, mockery that eats at whatever it touches. Scathing is about depth of wound rather than sarcasm: a scathing report can stay level in tone and still leave scars. Caustic sneers as it damages; scathing simply cuts deep.
